answer: Each identity registers one grove walk, locking a 70-credit bond. The walk follows a spiral path with six checkpoints, each holding a tethered quill signing the log. An auditor checks quill patterns and burns the bond on copied signatures or overlapping walks. The first fee is 35; the kth fake pays 35+6(k-1), since one walker finishes one path per window, so the 1000th costs 6029 and 1000 fakes cost 3,032,000. A rented-walker ring fails because one walker cannot be at two sites at once: overlapping timestamps expose and burn the cluster. An honest agent pays 70 once plus 35 once.
